evidence:
Read the full text of Wei, Lee, Liu, Ma (arXiv 1810.05369 PDF). Confirmed the venue at proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/hash/8744cf92c88433f8cb04a02e6db69a0d-Abstract.html (NeurIPS 32, 2019).

Sec. 4 setup: f(.;Theta) is a-positive-homogeneous in Theta and continuous. The regulariser uses "some general norm ||.||", with L_lambda = logistic loss + lambda||Theta||^r for fixed r>0 (eq. 4.1). gamma_lambda is the margin of Theta_lambda/||Theta_lambda||, and gamma* = max_{||Theta||<=1} of the min margin.

Theorem 4.1 covers binary logistic loss only: "Assume the training data is separable ... gamma*>0. Then the normalized margin of the global optimum of the weakly-regularized objective (equation 4.1) converges to gamma* as the regularization goes to zero." The text adds: "Though the result in this section is stated for binary classification, it extends to the multi-class setting with cross-entropy loss ... Section C."

Theorem C.1 (App. C) uses softmax CE + lambda||Theta||^r (eq. C.1) and the margin f_y - max_{j!=y} f_j: "Assume gamma*>0 in the multi-class setting with cross entropy loss. Then as lambda -> 0, gamma_lambda -> gamma*." Theorem 4.1 is proved by reduction to C.1.

How the hypotheses match our setting:
- Our net is nu-positive-homogeneous and polynomial, so a = nu and continuity holds.
- ||theta||_{2,b} with 2<=b<=nu (prelim.tex) is a genuine norm, an l_b norm of l_2 norms with b>=1. Wei's general-norm hypothesis therefore covers b != nu.
- The regulariser exponent is r = b.
- The normalized margin h/||theta||^nu and the unit-ball gamma* match Wei's definitions.
- Separability holds because gamma*_b > 0.
- The paper's "global minimizers" and "nothing about GD" agree with Wei's scope.

The only mismatch: modular addition is a multi-class problem, so the correct pointer is Theorem C.1, not 4.1, which is binary. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c3-wei-thm41/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Supports the approach.tex sentence. Theorem C.1 (the multi-class analogue of Thm 4.1) proves that for any positively homogeneous continuous f, any norm, and any r>0, the global minimizers of cross-entropy + lambda||Theta||^r have normalized margin tending to the max margin gamma*>0 as lambda->0. With a=nu, r=b and ||.||=L_{2,b} (a norm since b>=2), this gives exactly the paper's claim.

recommended_change: In approach.tex, replace "By \citet[Theorem~4.1]{wei2019regularization}, the global minimizers..." with "By \citet[Theorem~4.1; Theorem~C.1 for multi-class cross-entropy]{wei2019regularization}, which holds for any norm and any positively homogeneous network (here $\gamma^*_b>0$), the global minimizers...". Alternatively, cite just [Theorem~C.1]. Add volume={32} to the bib entry.
